caseStudies.title: The Governance & ROI Engine
caseStudies.headline: Optimizing enterprise intelligence via Copilot analytics.
caseStudies.action: Engineered a real-time dashboard for Copilot usage reporting and analysis — benchmarks, adoption trends, team-level comparisons and an ROI calculator built for CTOs and engineering managers.
caseStudies.metric: Identified a 25% license optimization opportunity and documented 15–35% operational cost reductions across engineering teams.
caseStudies.problem: Leadership was paying for AI seats without a clear picture of who used them, how, or what they were worth. The business case for AI investment was anecdotal.
approach: Pulled Copilot telemetry into a rolling 7/14/28-day reporting model across the enterprise.
Built views by language/IDE, model, team, and individual, with benchmarks against org averages.
Added an ROI tab that converts hours reclaimed into labor value against license cost.
Made the report printable for executive review so the numbers travel without the tool.
caseStudies.governance: Usage data is reported at team level for decisions; individual views exist to coach, not to rank.
caseStudies.imageAlt: Copilot analytics dashboard: enterprise overview with active users, apply rate, chat and agent adoption, daily active users and daily lines-of-code trend charts.

caseStudies.title: Building the Digital Workforce
caseStudies.headline: Scaling agentic capability via MCP training — the AI KT Series.
caseStudies.action: Architected an org-wide Knowledge Transfer series training engineers to build Model Context Protocol servers, Skills, and custom instructions — the human infrastructure that makes AI adoption stick.
caseStudies.metric: Accelerated the deployment of 10+ custom internal agent tools, reducing developer rote work by 40%.
caseStudies.problem: Engineers had AI assistants but no shared patterns for extending them. Every team reinvented prompts, and nobody owned when an agent should stop and ask.
approach: Designed a curriculum: MCP fundamentals → building tools → Skills and IDE optimization → agentic workflows.
Documented custom instructions that gate which skills an agent may use, per repo and per task.
Standardized Human-in-the-Loop checkpoints so every generated artifact has a named reviewer.
Turned workshop outputs into shipped internal tools, not slideware.
caseStudies.governance: Custom instructions define agent scope; HITL checkpoints are mandatory before anything leaves the developer's machine.

caseStudies.title: AI-Powered Developer Tooling
caseStudies.headline: Automating the SDLC via intelligent code agents.
caseStudies.action: Developed a suite of AI-integrated coding tools that streamline repository management and pull-request review.
caseStudies.metric: Shorter review cycles and consistent PR quality through structured, evidence-backed agent recommendations.
caseStudies.problem: PR review was the bottleneck: large diffs, inconsistent standards, and reviewers re-deriving context every time.
approach: Map: split each PR into file- and concern-level chunks and analyze them in parallel.
Reduce: merge findings into one evidence-backed report with a confidence score.
Align: check the report against repo conventions and team standards before surfacing it.
The agent recommends approve, reject or manual review — a human makes the call.
caseStudies.governance: The agent never merges. Low-confidence or security-relevant findings force manual review.

caseStudies.title: Figma → Jira / Wiki Automation
caseStudies.headline: Design context in, tickets and technical docs out.
caseStudies.action: LLM + Figma MCP + API integration that auto-generates Jira tickets and technical wiki documentation directly from design context. Owned end to end: product definition, stakeholder alignment with PMs and Scrum Masters, and engineering execution.
caseStudies.metric: Eliminates manual documentation labor between design and engineering across the org.
caseStudies.problem: Every design handoff meant hand-writing tickets and specs that drifted from the source of truth.
approach: Read component structure and annotations from Figma through MCP.
Generate structured tickets and wiki pages from that context with an LLM.
Route drafts to the PM for approval before anything is created in Jira.
caseStudies.governance: Drafts only — a PM approves before tickets are created.

caseStudies.title: QA Test Case Automation
caseStudies.headline: Test cases generated from Storybook through MCP.
caseStudies.action: Automated test case generation pipeline via Storybook and MCP servers, reducing manual QA effort while maintaining quality standards team-wide.
caseStudies.metric: Reduced manual QA effort while keeping quality standards consistent across teams.
caseStudies.problem: QA wrote test cases by hand from component states that already existed, fully described, in Storybook.
approach: Expose component stories and their states to an agent through MCP.
Generate test cases per state (default, active, loading, error).
QA reviews and accepts cases into the suite.
caseStudies.governance: Generated cases are proposals; QA owns acceptance.

governance.intro: Autonomy is earned, scoped and reversible. Every agent I deploy sits at an explicit level on this ladder, with a named human above it.

levels.name: Suggest
levels.body: Agent drafts; human writes. Default for anything customer-facing.

levels.name: Draft & route
levels.body: Agent produces an artifact and routes it to a named reviewer (tickets, test cases, PR reports).

levels.name: Act in sandbox
levels.body: Agent executes inside a scoped environment with gated skills and logged tool calls.

levels.name: Act with hard stops
levels.body: Agent runs end to end; defined hard stops (security, money, people data) always escalate.

principles: Every agent has a named human owner.
Hard stops for security, spend, and personal data are non-negotiable.
Tool calls are logged and reviewable.
Efficiency claims are validated against telemetry, not anecdotes.

builds.name: RepoHQ
builds.tagline: Portfolio intelligence for every repo I own — and an agent factory that acts on it.
builds.summary: RepoHQ syncs all of my GitHub repositories, scores their health, and turns that into ranked, quantified next actions. An AI advisor proposes the work; a sandboxed agent factory runs it on free models and judges every change before it lands.
highlights: 7-factor health score per repo (activity, security, deployments, docs, tests, dependencies, quality) and a single 0–100 portfolio score with weekly delta
AI Advisor ranks the top 5 actions with expected score deltas, then tracks predicted vs. actual outcomes to improve itself
Agent execution: advisor actions and skills are queued to a factory that writes code in a sandbox and gates every change
MCP server with 14 tools exposes portfolio context and the agent lifecycle to Claude Code and other MCP clients
Revenue and lifecycle tracking (MRR/ARR, Stripe sync, 8 stages from Idea to Archived) plus an opt-in public portfolio page

builds.name: AI Radar
builds.tagline: Weekly, signal-based rankings for 150 AI tools — no opinions, just data.
builds.summary: AI Radar crawls six public sources every week and turns raw signals into a RadarScore (0–100) for each AI tool, with sub-score breakdowns, score history, movers and head-to-head comparisons. A Claude enrichment agent writes the comparisons.
highlights: Event-driven Inngest pipeline: weekly cron fans out to 6 crawler agents (GitHub, Reddit, Hacker News, ArXiv, G2, changelogs)
RadarScore = 5 equally weighted, percentile-normalized sub-scores: buzz, adoption momentum, developer sentiment, recency, enterprise readiness
Missing signals redistribute weight instead of penalizing a tool
Claude enrichment agent generates tool comparisons; pages revalidate after each run
Leaderboard, category views, top movers, tool 'graveyard' and per-tool radar + trend charts

builds.name: Open Adventure
builds.tagline: “Skyscanner Explore” for the outdoors — discover where to go, not just research a place you picked.
builds.summary: Open Adventure (working name Travel Roamer) is a discovery platform for outdoor trips. A full-screen map with vibe and trip filters leads to destination and trail pages built on a provenance-backed content model, where every fact is sourced, attributed and freshness-gated.
highlights: Discovery across 28 published national parks and 165 trails, with vibe, activity, trip length, season, budget and permit filters
Search with zero-result relaxation, so a narrow query widens instead of returning nothing
Five live data sources including NPS, OpenStreetMap trails, Open-Meteo forecasts and Wikimedia photos, all attributed and freshness-gated
Trail pages with route maps and an interactive elevation chart linked to the map; editorial admin with AI-assisted drafting
105 unit tests and 16 end-to-end tests, including axe accessibility checks, run in CI

builds.name: Open Fly Travel Assistant
builds.tagline: Group trip planning where AI reads the booking confirmations for you.
builds.summary: A collaborative travel app: plan trips together, drop in PDFs or screenshots of booking confirmations and let Claude extract the events, then split costs across the group with real-time sync.
highlights: Itinerary in four views: list, Kanban, block and calendar
Document parsing: upload PDFs or images and Claude extracts event details automatically
Budget tracker with four split modes (equal, exact, percentage, shares), balances and settle-up
Real-time collaboration via Supabase, plus read-only public share links
Maps, flight lookups and web push notifications

builds.name: Roots & Branches
builds.tagline: An interactive family tree you can explore, enrich and share.
builds.summary: A full-stack genealogy platform: build and visualize a family lineage as an interactive graph, map ancestors' journeys, attach photos from Google, and collaborate with relatives — with subscriptions, AI biographies and role-based access built in.
highlights: Interactive React Flow graph with standard, ancestor-fan, descendant and event-chart views
Geographic history on heatmap and marker maps
Google Drive / Photos integration through a second OAuth grant
Stripe subscription tiers and AI-generated biographies
Role-based access control with audit logging; a full mock mode for development without external services
